title: Touring big bands in New Orleans
summary: George E. Lee, J.C. Beaton, Ellington, Chick Webb, Trent and Milton Larkins.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: What about the bands coming in from out of town?

Well, the first big band came to New Orleans. I know it was the first one. It was in the, in the, in the, in the, in the, in the early 30's. George E. Lee from Kansas City. Oh yeah? Was that a good band? Ooh, yes indeed. That's the first time I ever heard big time music. Mmhmm. And then, Belton. From Florida.
Belton? That's entirely new to me. I never heard of him before in my life. Belton. Belton. Featuring T Hound Slim.

That's the second big band invented here. T what? T Hound Slim, that's the first. T Hound Slim? Yeah, he used to dance and singing. Dance in front of the band. That's all, let's dance. Mmhmm. Then I forgot about Walter Barnes. Mmhmm. He was coming in. Then, uh, Nat Tolles started coming. Mmhmm. Nat Tolles.
Mmhmm.
Then Eli Rice started coming.
You ever heard of him? I've heard of him. Never heard of him. Never heard of Nat Tolles, either.
Yeah. And Duke made his appearance on the Pelican. Oh. Duke Ellington. Oh. Oh. Then come Chick Webb. Mmhmm. Then Father O'Hinds, he came. That's many of many. That's many of many.
That reminds me, why did they call the guy T Hound Slim? I don't know.
That was, that's one of the greatest bands I ever heard. Mmhmm. J.C. Belton from West Palm Beach, Florida. Mmhmm.
Well, I guess he had plenty of people down there with money in West Palm Beach. I think that's plenty of people.
Yeah, he had a 15 piece band. That's the man who wanted to take Chester away from him. Which Chester?
Chester's.

Chester's ours. Chester told him no, he wasn't gonna leave in yours. At that time, Kid Rainier was playing on that story, featuring, what's the point of the name? Alto. Teddy. Theda. Theda O'Painal. We can put that old point of on the alto. Mmhmm. Theda. Chester. Chester on bass. Randy had a woman, I never, never did know her name, playing the piano. And his brother Joe, and they had Henry Harden on it. She's a tenor. They used a couple of nights out.
Hmm? Go ahead, nothing. Did what? Nothing. I'm about to fall asleep. I'm tired, I was out late last night. You tired? Yeah. Yeah. Shots worked on their job for us too. Mmhmm. Mmhmm. Mmhmm.
Yeah this was a hard job to build for the trumpet players. Mmhmm. Mmhmm. Now, um, did Larry have a big band then?
I forgot about him, yeah.
No Larry had the band but- Mmhmm. Mmhmm. Mmhmm.

Mmhmm. Mmhmm. Mmhmm. Was another Larry not here? Jimmy. Jimmy Larry. He did. The, the, the, the cornet player had the band. Larry inherited that band from his brother. Oh. Jimmy Larry had the band. Did you ever hear a Don Albums band? Yeah, I know. They were, they came in, they came here in the early, early thirties too. Alvin Alcon was in that band. Got a trombone player named Geechee. I can't talk about the name of Fernandez. I believe he's from here. Fred Nandese, huh? Yeah, I know something like that. Yeah, he's from here. Tell me, last thing I heard he had lost his mind. Yeah, I think he died in the hospital. Yeah.
Yeah. All that kind of stuff. It was T Holder that I wanted to ask you about. Did you ever hear T Holder's band out of Texas? Never heard of them. They're supposed to be tough. I think he

sort of tied up with some of the Kansas City guys. I heard Alcon's, Alcon's Trent. Oh yeah? That was a good band. He came out of Texas. Did he come here? Uh-huh. Trent. Did he come to New Orleans? Yeah, Trent. Trent came here. Well, when did he come here? I'm trying to remember when he was. Trent came here in the middle thirties. I can't remember when he went down. Trent came here. Milton Larkins. Oh yeah. Milton Larkins was here every week. Carolina Cotton Pickers.
Did you know the guys in the Carolina Cotton Pickers?
I only know Seabrook. Who is Seabrook? He was a trumpet player. When he leaves, the notes would be up in the ceiling. Just whistle. You know like Cat Anderson do? He whistle trumpet all night.
